amendments.rule: **The *that* of a presentative `הָיָה` belongs to that verb, and is not `added`.** The ASV renders `וַיְהִי` and `וְהָיָה` with a frame — *And it came to pass … that*, *And it shall come to pass … that* — and the frame's complementizer is part of what the verb is rendered by, exactly as rule 21's dummy subject is. It joins the `הָיָה` unit, headed as that unit already heads. The unit may be discontinuous under rule 25 where a temporal phrase stands inside the frame: `וְהָיָה אַחֲרֵי כֵן` → *And it shall come to pass afterward, that* gives `הָיָה` both *it shall come to pass* and *that*, while `אַחֲרֵי כֵן` keeps *afterward*. **Where the apodosis opens with its own waw, that waw carries the *that* instead** and the verb keeps only *it came to pass*; and where the ASV writes no *that* at all there is nothing to place. Read which of the three the verse is rather than reaching for the verb every time. **But read where the ASV has written the word before handing it to that waw.** The waw carries the *that* only where the ASV writes it at the head of the apodosis; where the ASV instead writes it immediately after the frame, ahead of the temporal phrase or of a temporal clause carrying a subordinator of its own, the word stands inside the frame rather than at the apodosis's head, the frame keeps it under this rule's first sentence, and the apodosis waw, for which the ASV has then written no connective, is `unrepresented` under rule 14. `וַיְהִי כֶּאֱמֹר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶל־הָעָם וְשִׁבְעָה הַכֹּהֲנִים ... עָבְרוּ` → *And it was so,* ***that*** *when Joshua had spoken unto the people, the seven priests ... passed on* gives *it was so that* to `הָיָה` and *when* to the `כְּ` under rule 52, leaving that waw nothing, while `וַיְהִי כִשְׁמֹעַ הָעָם ... וַיָּרִיעוּ הָעָם` → *And it came to pass, when the people heard ...,* ***that*** *the people shouted* writes its one *that* at the head of the apodosis and gives it to the waw that opens it. Read the English word order, since what tells the two apart is where the ASV has put the word and not that a waw stands in the apodosis at all. **And where the ASV writes no complementizer at the apodosis head, the frame has none to place.** A subordinator the ASV supplies for a temporal clause the Hebrew writes asyndetically is not the frame's: no morpheme stands in that clause to carry it, so it is its own `added` unit under rule 55, and the apodosis waw is `unrepresented` as before. `וַיְהִי בַּפַּעַם הַשְּׁבִיעִית תָּקְעוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים בַּשּׁוֹפָרוֹת וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ` → *And it came to pass at the seventh time,* ***when*** *the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said* leaves that *when* `added`, while the same word is the preposition's wherever a `כְּ` or a `בְּ` stands to carry it, as in the two examples above. Count the ASV's subordinators against the morphemes that could carry them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s. **And where what stands inside the frame is not a phrase but a temporal clause the ASV writes with a relative or complementizer of its own, the frame's *that* is the one standing at the head of the apodosis, never the first one written.** Read the Hebrew for where the apodosis begins and count the ASV's *that*s against the clauses that license them, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s: a *that* introducing the temporal clause answers to whatever morpheme rules 52 and 19 put it on, and only the *that* the ASV writes before the apodosis is the frame's. `וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת־בָּנָיו ... לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר` → *then it shall be in the day* ***that*** *he causeth his sons to inherit that which he hath,* ***that*** *he may not make the son of the beloved the first born* gives the second *that* to `הָיָה`, discontinuous across the whole temporal clause under rule 25, and the first to the infinitive construct, exactly as rule 52 leaves *when they shall make* to the infinitive of `בְּיוֹם הֵעָשׂוֹתוֹ` where the `בְּ` and the construct noun each already hold an English word of their own. Do not mark the apodosis *that* `added` under rule 55 on the ground that no conjunction stands in its clause: the frame licenses it, and a frame whose complementizer has been spent on the temporal clause will always leave one over.
amendments.why: JOS.6 met two shapes the rule's waw sentence did not consider, and read literally the rule decides both wrongly. In JOS.6.8 the ASV writes one *that*, immediately after *And it was so* and ahead of a temporal clause carrying its own *when*, while the Hebrew apodosis opens with a waw; handing that word to the waw would place it before the very clause it is said to open, and JOS.6.5 writes the identical English where the apodosis has no waw at all and the frame keeps the word uncontroversially. So the placement of the word, not the presence of a waw, is what the rule must turn on. In JOS.6.16 the ASV writes no complementizer for the apodosis and supplies a *when* for an asyndetic temporal clause; the rule's own closing paragraph makes the frame's *that* the one at the apodosis head and sends a temporal-clause subordinator to whatever morpheme carries it, so with no morpheme there rule 55 governs and the word is `added` — which JOS.6.20 confirms inside the same chapter, writing that *when* for a present `כְּ` while its *that* goes to the apodosis waw. Both additions are qualifications of the existing sentences in their own terms; nothing already in the rule is dropped or reversed.

conventions: The chapter's five הָיָה frames are read by where the ASV wrote the complementizer, not by whether the apodosis has a waw: 6.5 and 6.8 keep *that* with the frame, because it stands immediately after *it shall be* / *it was so* and ahead of the temporal material; 6.15 and 6.20 give *that* to the apodosis waw, because it stands at that clause's head; and 6.16 writes none for the apodosis, so its waw is `unrepresented` and the *when* it supplies for the asyndetic תָּקְעוּ clause is `added`. Where a כְּ stands (6.5, 6.8, 6.20) it takes the *when* under rule 52.

תַּחְתֶּיהָ → *flat* (6.5, 6.20): the one English word goes to תַּחַת and the 3fs suffix is its own `unrepresented` unit, since *flat* carries nothing of the suffix and rule 30's condition is unmet for it. The ASV's marginal *Hebrew in its place* is what the fused reading would rest on; it is not taken. BSB represents the suffix in both verses.

A jussive the ASV expands with a *let* frame keeps that frame with the verb whose mood it renders, discontinuous around an intervening subject (rule 17): יִשְׂאוּ → *let ... bear* (6.6), יַעֲבֹר → *let ... pass on* (6.7), תַשְׁמִיעוּ → *let ... be heard* (6.10). The *let* is not rule 20's supplied lexical verb and is never `added`.

The italic *the priests* the ASV supplies as subject of the closing participial clause is `added` in each of 6.9, 6.13 and 6.20 (rules 7, 17); it is not folded into the infinitive absolute or the participle standing beside it.

The infinitive absolute of הָלַךְ is read by what the ASV spends on it: recast as a finite clause it takes the whole clause as its own unit, הָלוֹךְ → *as they went* (6.9, 6.13), headed on the lexical verb; written as a distinct adverb it is rule 56's, הָלוֹךְ → *continually* (6.13). The waw between two infinitives absolute is `unrepresented` where the ASV writes no connective (6.9, 6.13).

Rule 31's tie-break is settled inside this chapter for two lemmas: the ASV writes a bare *ram's* for יוֹבֵל (6.5) and a bare *young* for נַעַר (6.21), so *rams horns* heads on *rams* (6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 6.13) and *young men* on *young* (6.23), the accompanying noun being the supplied generic.

report: Cross-verse check: the הָיָה frame is the chapter's only genuine split. JOS.6.5 and JOS.6.8 keep the frame's complementizer because the ASV writes the *that* immediately after the frame; JOS.6.15 and JOS.6.20 give it to the apodosis waw because the ASV writes it at the head of the apodosis. JOS.6.16 writes no complementizer for the apodosis at all and supplies a *when* for a temporal clause the Hebrew writes asyndetically (תָּקְעוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים), which no morpheme licenses; it is patched to `added` under rule 55, and the apodosis waw stays `unrepresented` as in JOS.6.8. JOS.6.20 is the decisive in-chapter parallel: there the same *when* answers to a written כְּ while the *that* goes to the apodosis waw, and JOS.6.18 already marks a supplied *when* `added`.

JOS.6.8 sits against a literal reading of rule 45's sentence handing the *that* to an apodosis waw, and it is kept as aligned rather than patched: the word stands before the temporal clause, inside the frame, and JOS.6.5 writes the identical English where the apodosis has no waw at all. Rule 45 is amended so that it turns on where the ASV wrote the word rather than on whether a waw stands in the apodosis, and so that it disposes of the JOS.6.16 shape explicitly.

Everything else the candidate table flags is licensed by the ASV rather than a split: הַ as *the*, *that* or `unrepresented` (6.22 attributive relative vs. 6.23 substantival vs. rule 47 agreement articles), בְּ written vs. silenced by rule 40's promoted object after *blew*, הָלַךְ as *went*, *came* and *followed*, אֵת H853 vs. the preposition H854 (6.17, 6.27), the מִן … עַד range in 6.21, and the determiner counts in 6.15, 6.25 and 6.26, which are uniform. The three פַּעַם אֶחָת → *once* fusions, the three supplied-italic *the priests* `added` units (6.9, 6.13, 6.20) and the three supplied object pronouns (6.11, 6.18, 6.26) each agree with themselves.

Head choices are corroborated inside the chapter rather than assumed: the ASV writes a bare *ram's* for יוֹבֵל (6.5) and a bare *young* for נַעַר (6.21), which is rule 31's tie-break for heading *rams horns* on *rams* and *young men* on *young* in 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 6.13 and 6.23.

BSB: no genuine error. The C, To, Td, Rd and R class disagreements are the documented convention difference (BSB attaches a function morpheme to its host where the ASV writes nothing for it). The two individual flags are contract-determined: the suffix of תַּחְתֶּיהָ (6.5, 6.20) is not carried by *flat*, so rule 30's condition is unmet for it and rule 22 leaves it `unrepresented`; and the resuming הוּא of 6.19 is rule 20's tripartite clause, where the copula goes to the predicate and the pronoun is the unrendered occurrence. Nothing was changed to move the aggregate.
